Web crawlers discover pages by following hyperlinks, fetching documents over HTTP, and storing their content for later processing. A modern crawler must respect politeness delays, deduplicate near-identical pages, render JavaScript-heavy applications, and prioritise the frontier so that important pages are refreshed first. Once the text has been extracted, it is split into chunks, embedded into a dense vector space, and written to an approximate nearest neighbour index.
